SINNER: Sacrifice for Redemption - The Game Where You Level Backwords

Game Description

SINNER is a third person action RPG with a theme of sin and sacrifice, made by Chinese developer Dark Star. The unique selling point is that you level down and get weaker as you progress through the game, the opposite of the traditional RPG character arc.

There are 7 bosses, each based off of one of the seven deadly sins, and in order to unlock each boss fight, you must sacrifice some of your power and abilities. Sometimes this can be as straightforward as losing health and stamina or charges for consumable items. Sometimes it adds new mechanics to the game like causing you to get winded if you dodge while out of stamina.

Sinner has snappy, satisfying 'Souls-like' combat, and some really interesting encounters. It a straight boss rush with no trash mobs, so don't expect to get more than a handful of hours out of it, but it has a lot of heart and polish.

Episode Topics

Joseph Hewes writes to Samuel Johnston. Britain's act prohibiting all trade and commerce with the Colonies and making American property liable to seizure and confiscation, will make a breach between the two countries that can not be reconciled. Nothing is left but to fight, and for that we're not well provided. Nor is there unanimity in the Councils. Some wish strongly for Independence immediately while others wish to have the opinion of their constituents. Yesterday, Congress authorized privateers can cruise against British vessels.

Francis Lewis writes to William Livingston. Mr. John Griffiths, owner of a foundry, issued a complaint that others who contracted with the committee in Philadelphia got higher prices than he did for similar goods. He will not fall back on delivery of his goods - but this illustrates how necessary it is for committees of Congress to be wary of paying high prices.

Maryland Delegates to Maryland Council of Safety. Folks, we got gunpowder and arms from Capt Tibbit, along with gunpowder advanced by Congress and lended by others, on a boat over to Christina Bridge. From there it went to Baltimore by wagons. Intelligence reports HMS Otter, a 14 gun ship of war, and supporting ships have arrived at the Patapsco river. Individuals are trying to buy gunpowder for themselves or their county, but it is difficult.

Richard Smith recounts happenings in Continental Congress. Fortifications are authorized to be built in Canada not to exceed $100,000. Rutledge moved that Magaws Regiment be armed with Pikes since they have no guns, and other regiments want in on that action too.
